```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
library(RiccatiSolver)
```

## L'équation

On étudie $y' = a(x)\,y^2 + b(x)\,y + c(x)$. Prenons $y' = y^2 - 2y + 1$ avec $y(0) = 0$,
dont la solution exacte est $y = x/(x+1)$.

```{r exemple}
eq  <- riccati(a = 1, b = -2, c = 1)
sol <- solve_riccati(eq, y0 = 0, interval = c(0, 5))
sol
plot_riccati(sol)
```

## Comparer plusieurs conditions initiales

```{r comparaison}
compare_riccati(eq, y0 = c(-1, 0, 0.5, 2), interval = c(0, 3), ylim = c(-2, 3))
```

## Champ de directions

```{r champ}
riccati_field(eq, xlim = c(0, 5), ylim = c(-1, 3), solution = sol)
```

## Transformation en équation linéaire

```{r transformation}
tr <- riccati_transform(eq, y0 = 0, interval = c(0, 5))
tr
max(abs(tr$solution$data$y - sol$data$y))
```

## Explosion en temps fini

Pour $y' = y^2$ avec $y(0) = 1$, la solution $1/(1-x)$ explose en $x = 1$.

```{r explosion}
eq2  <- riccati(a = 1, b = 0, c = 0)
sol2 <- solve_riccati(eq2, y0 = 1, interval = c(0, 3))
riccati_study(sol2)
plot_riccati(sol2)
```
